name: Babrius
bio: Babrius (also written Babrias) was a Greek fabulist who put the fables traditionally ascribed to Aesop into choliambic verse, probably in the 2nd century AD, though his date is uncertain and almost nothing is known of his life. His prologues address a boy named Branchus and a prince called Alexander.

His verse was known only from scattered quotations until the Greek scholar Minoides Mynas brought home a transcript of a manuscript found on Mount Athos, published in Paris in 1844. It holds 123 fables arranged alphabetically and breaks off at the letter O; more were later recovered from other sources. Sir George Cornewall Lewis edited the text in England in 1846.
